## Usage and eight-document index

| Document | Purpose / reader |
|---|---|
| README.md | Index, provenance, self-check and limitations |
| modules.md | Modules, boundaries and executable units |
| architecture.md | Calling mechanism, identity and behavior switches |
| extension.md | Implementation starting points and change routing |
| api.md | Actual callable surface |
| capabilities.md | Product behavior, live requirements and conflicts |
| building-blocks.md | Assets implementers can reuse |
| testing.md | Test definitions and smoke/review starting points |

Product starts with capabilities; implement starts with extension and building-blocks; smoke starts with testing; review checks source records and conflicts. No additional knowledge body is included. Documents use English to match the repository README and specification. Source-status and verification labels retain the skill's canonical vocabulary.

## Inferences, unknowns, conflicts and uncovered material

- `capabilities:F003`: exact matching in code and tests conflicts with the live prefix-search requirement. Both sources remain authoritative evidence of their respective actual/required behavior; implementation is not declared compliant.
- `capabilities:F004`: README references unavailable `docs/retired-runtime.md`. Its contents and historical runtime details remain [待确认]. The actual filesystem absence was checked, not inferred from Git tracking.
- `capabilities:F001`: upstream lineage is [待确认]; no upstream implementation or provenance is identified by the available project metadata.
- `extension:F001`, `extension:F004`: extension and routing advice is explicitly inference from the current small repository, not an existing generator or authorization rule.
- `testing:F001`: the unittest discovery command is derived from imports and layout; it was not executed. Packaging/build behavior, deployed environment, malformed-input behavior beyond direct language semantics, and platform compatibility were not runtime-verified.
- `testing:F004`: no repository regression command or acceptance harness was established. Private engine state and configuration were not read to manufacture one.
- Existing repository contribution/commit rules are missing within the inspected scope (`extension:F003`). Conversation-supplied instructions are separate from repository facts.
- Invocation provenance discrepancy: the request lists skill SHA-256 `2d2e25d3e5128f44cddbac16d12523329385db40a0d74f79f1f1fc8e1efc8cb6`, while both local `.claude/skills/foundation-survey/SKILL.md` and `.codex/skills/foundation-survey/SKILL.md` hash to `59398379c962dfdf4ab29a43e5b719c9fa0f011717470a6a1fc21c001a782f10`. The local skill declares 1.1.0; this survey followed the supplied instructions and read the local skill and references. The reason for the fingerprint mismatch remains [待确认]. These untracked files are not attributed to the observed commit.

## Directed checks

- Baseline: safely read only baseline metadata fields; `baseline_version` agrees with the payload, and independently read `source_head` equals the observed Git HEAD. The ignored `.storyloop/` directory actually exists. No private configuration/state was opened.
- Version/worktree: repeated `git rev-parse HEAD` and `git status --short` returned the same SHA and untracked skill directories. Source and tests had no reported tracked changes.
- Identity/rejection: reopened app/catalog.py:1-3; no identity input or authorization branch exists. Python input failures are not authorization failures.
- Switch defaults: reopened app/catalog.py:1-3 and pyproject.toml:1-4; no runtime switch is defined or consumed, so no configurable default or deployed value is asserted.
- Test isolation: reopened tests/test_catalog.py:4-8; synthetic local fixture, no accounts, database or reset mechanism.
- Writes: lookup constructs a list without explicit persistence or input mutation. Arbitrary caller-provided objects may have effects in iteration/access/equality; no universal purity guarantee is claimed. Survey issued read-only inspection and metadata computation commands only.
- Conflict/errata: reopened both sides of the prefix/exact mismatch. `openspec/foundation/` does not yet exist, so there is no existing foundation claim to quote as errata. The live specification conflict is recorded in capabilities, not rewritten or dismissed.
- Coverage: all eight requested files and all template coverage categories are present. Non-applicable service/frontend/database sections retain scope explanations. No credentials or secret runtime configuration were opened or reproduced.

## Refresh and review

Scope: project README, pyproject, complete app and tests source, live search specification, ignore rules, safe baseline metadata, skill instructions/references, and explicit filesystem presence checks. Repository files were not written. The engine must install and process the returned documents; this response does not establish BASE acceptance.

Recheck affected facts after upstream synchronization or a mechanism-changing BASE. Maintainers should review after 10 completed changes or 30 days from this self-check, whichever comes first (time trigger: 2026-11-20). This is a manual convention, not an installed scheduler. Outstanding work: resolve the search requirement conflict, recover historical documentation if needed, establish upstream/build/regression provenance, explain the skill fingerprint discrepancy, and obtain independent review. Old undocumented knowledge is not retroactively marked verified.
